title: SharePoint: FAQ web part becomes non-AI, with AI FAQ generation in Copilot in SharePoint
summary: The briefing accurately reports the FAQ authoring change and Microsoft's rollout notice. Its site control and Copilot licensing statements are documented, and it preserves the uncertainty about FAQ-specific credit consumption and GCC availability.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe this FAQ web part authoring change in November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint FAQ web part authoring admin settings Set-SPOSite; SharePoint FAQ generation Copilot Credits licensing. Read Copilot in SharePoint getting-started and returned Set-SPOSite excerpts; no FAQ-change documentation.

claims.claim: The documented Copilot in SharePoint licensing model is mixed, combining licence-included everyday work and credit-billed advanced work.
claims.quote: Copilot in SharePoint uses a hybrid business model. Everyday individual productivity is included with the Microsoft 365 Copilot license. Advanced work requires usage-based billing and consumes Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is enabled in SharePoint admin center through Sites > Active sites > site > Settings > Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote: In the SharePoint admin center, expand Sites and select Active sites. Select the site you want to configure. Open the Settings tab, and then turn Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot on.

claims.claim: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true enables Restricted Content Discovery for the site.
claims.quote: Enable Restricted Content Discovery for a site ... Use PowerShell ... Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true

claims.where: controls[0].governs; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is an existing site-level setting that makes Copilot in SharePoint and AI actions disappear from the site.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery is an existing setting that's respected. If it's enabled on a site, Copilot in SharePoint and AI actions don't appear on that site. This rule applies regardless of your other availability settings.

claims.claim: Only SharePoint administrators manage Restricted Content Discovery by default.
claims.quote: By default, only SharePoint administrators can manage Restricted Content Discovery.

claims.claim: Management of Restricted Content Discovery can optionally be delegated to site administrators.
claims.quote: When delegation is enabled, site administrators can manage Restricted Content Discovery for their sites.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery requires the organisation to have a Microsoft Copilot licence and meet the cited page's prerequisites.
claims.quote: Review the SharePoint Advanced Management prerequisites ... Ensure your organization has a Microsoft Copilot license. ... Review your organization's existing categories, and if necessary, add categories.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery removes AI entry points including the Copilot button and Create pages with AI.
claims.quote: Users don't see entry points such as the Copilot button, AI actions menus (including creating agents), or Create pages with AI.

claims.claim: No FAQ-authoring-specific admin setting is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint FAQ web part authoring admin settings Set-SPOSite. Read returned Set-SPOSite excerpts, Restricted Content Discovery, Copilot in SharePoint getting-started and authoring overview; no FAQ-specific admin setting or direct FAQ-web-part effect described.

claims.claim: Learn says preview PowerShell availability settings remain effective until November 1, 2026.
claims.quote: Existing PowerShell settings remain in effect until November 1, 2026. After November 1, 2026, manage availability by using Site AI settings and Restricted Content Discovery.

claims.claim: The cited Restricted Content Discovery page does not describe its direct effect on the FAQ web part itself.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint FAQ web part authoring admin settings Set-SPOSite. Read the complete Restricted Content Discovery page and Copilot in SharePoint availability section; neither describes a direct effect on the FAQ web part.

claims.claim: After November 1, 2026, Learn directs administrators to manage Copilot in SharePoint availability with Site AI settings and Restricted Content Discovery.
claims.quote: After November 1, 2026, manage availability by using Site AI settings and Restricted Content Discovery.
